title: KMS chaos failover harness and compact evidence bundler
creator: Diego Alvarez
description: Build a repeatable chaos-testing harness that simulates realistic KMS/HSM failover scenarios across regions and tenant configurations, and implement a Compact Evidence Bundler (CEB) that produces signed, compressed rotation and access evidence artifacts for auditors. Goal: prove that key rotation and wrap/unwrap workflows remain correct under transient KMS errors, region failovers, and during dual-KMS migration, while minimizing the storage footprint and ingestion time of audit evidence. Deliverables: (1) chaos harness with scenario definitions and automation, (2) evidence bundler service that aggregates rotation logs, wraps them with a deterministic envelope, compresses, and signs with a non-customer root for submission to the compliance pipeline, (3) observable dashboards and health checks, (4) test matrix documenting coverage per-customer and per-deployment-mode (hosted / dedicated / private). This ticket focuses on the first implementation slice (harness + basic bundler output format).
acceptance_criteria: Chaos harness can run 10 predefined scenarios (regional KMS outage, HSM latency spikes, KEK provider failover, truncated responses) against a staging fleet and report pass/fail per-tenant

Compact Evidence Bundler emits a signed tar.gz per rotation window that contains a manifest.json, rotated key metadata, rotation proofs (wrap/unwrap events), and the minimal tokenized audit pointer format
Produced evidence artifacts are no larger than 20% of equivalent raw logs when run against the sample 10k-req dataset
End-to-end test shows that a consumer (audit-ingest pipeline) can verify signature and parse the compact bundle within 5s
No unhandled leaks: chaos harness must not leave ephemeral keys in production; all simulated KEKs are scoped to the test namespace and cleaned up
Security review completed and automated signing key stored in HSM with rotation policy; doc updated with threat model notes
